newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 6.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 6. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Interior Minister Yogie Suardi Memet said the government was not responsible for the drop in the shares of votes obtained by the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) in the May 29 general election. The PDI has so far only secured 10 seats in the House of Representatives, less than the required minimum of 11 seats.

Television actress Zarina was sentenced to four years in jail for being in possession of 29,677 Ecstasy pills at her house. The court said she violated the 1992 Health Law by keeping the drugs in a safe at her house. The maximum penalty is 15 years.

PT Bimantara Cakra Nusa of Indonesia and Hyundai Motor Company of South Korea have formed a joint venture to set up an automotive manufacturing plant in Purwakarta, West Java, to produce Bimantara cars. The Bimantara Group is chaired by Bambang Trihatmodjo, President Suharto's second son.

Indonesia is seeking to obtain $5 billion in loans from the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) this year. Indonesia secured $5.26 billion in foreign loans last year, consisting of $2.563 billion from 18 CGI countries and $2.696 billion from international funding agencies.
